title: Choose where modalities should meet
description: Select a workload, fusion boundary, and token budget. The lab compares task fit, cross-modal interaction, precomputation, and degraded-input behavior without pretending to predict hardware latency.
note: The fit score is a transparent teaching heuristic. Benchmark candidate models on the target data, runtime, and hardware before making a production decision.

workloads.label: Cross-modal catalog search
workloads.detail: Index product images once, then retrieve them from short text queries.

workloads.label: Grounded visual support
workloads.detail: Answer a question by locating evidence in an uploaded product image.

workloads.label: Meeting evidence search
workloads.detail: Combine an audio transcript with slides that may arrive late or be absent.

workloads.label: Warehouse inspection
workloads.detail: Combine camera evidence with telemetry while preserving an explicit safe fallback.

architectures.label: Shared-space dual encoder
architectures.detail: Encode modalities independently and compare their normalized embeddings.
architectures.degradedBehavior: Either encoder can be monitored separately; the paired task cannot run when its required side is absent.

architectures.label: Token-level cross-attention
architectures.detail: Let visual and language tokens exchange evidence before the task output is produced.
architectures.degradedBehavior: Rich interaction depends on both token streams; missing-input behavior must be trained and evaluated explicitly.

architectures.label: Late fusion with a gate
architectures.detail: Keep modality-specific predictions separate, then combine or abstain with an availability-aware gate.
architectures.degradedBehavior: The gate can route around a missing path, lower authority, or abstain instead of silently substituting evidence.
